precepts.why:
The angel measures the whole compass round about, five hundred reeds on the east, five hundred on the north, five hundred on the south, five hundred on the west, about fifty-five hundred feet per side, with a wall round about “to make a separation between the sanctuary and the profane place.” Why does the Father require such careful preparation, rehearsed in such detail? “For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the Lord.”

That is above our pay grade. The Most High's thoughts and ways are higher than ours, so the reason for such exact preparation belongs to Him. We are to follow and learn.

What the measurements do tell us is where this is pointing: the kingdom. The temple will be established again with the same measurements given to King Solomon, done all over again.

precepts.why:
“And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls, and their kings shall minister unto thee: for in my wrath I smote thee, but in my favour have I had mercy on thee.” The wall round about, five hundred reeds long and five hundred broad, will be built by the sons of strangers.

The measurements in such detail point to the kingdom, when the temple is established again with the same measurements given to King Solomon. The other nations build it, and their kings minister; Israel's working days are over. In His wrath He smote us, but in His favour He has mercy on us.

points: Ezekiel is brought into the outer court toward the north, into the chamber over against the separate place, a hundred cubits long and fifty broad, about a hundred feet by seventy feet. Gallery is against gallery in three stories.

note.label: Ezekiel 42: The Priests' Chambers and the Separation of the Sanctuary

points: Before the chambers is a walk of ten cubits breadth inward, a way of one cubit, with doors toward the north, about fifteen feet and a foot and a half. The upper chambers are shorter because the galleries take away more from them, and the building has no pillars like the courts. An entry on the east side leads into them from the outer court.

note.label: Ezekiel 42: The Priests' Chambers and the Separation of the Sanctuary

points: The angel tells Ezekiel the north chambers and the south chambers before the separate place are holy chambers where the priests who approach the Lord shall eat the most holy things and lay the meat offering, the sin offering, and the trespass offering, because the place is holy.

note.label: Ezekiel 42: The Priests' Chambers and the Separation of the Sanctuary

points: When the priests enter, they shall not go out into the outer court until they lay aside the garments in which they minister, for those garments are holy. They put on other garments before they approach the things that are for the people. These are the laws the Levite priests are to follow.

note.label: Ezekiel 42: The Priests' Chambers and the Separation of the Sanctuary

points: When the angel finishes measuring the inner house, he brings Ezekiel out by the east gate and measures the whole compass round about, five hundred reeds on the east side, five hundred on the north, five hundred on the south, and five hundred on the west, about fifty-five hundred feet per side.
